condition: dayjs.duration(ms) built from a diff spanning months/years splits the milliseconds using fixed average month/year lengths, so years/months/days come out inconsistent with the calendar (e.g. 2023 full year gives 0 years 12 months 4 days).
workaround: Get calendar parts directly with end.diff(start, 'year'/'month'/'day') instead of turning a millisecond diff into a duration and reading its years()/months()/days().
